name: Diriyah
headline: The Birthplace of the Saudi State
overview: Founded in 1446, Diriyah became the capital of the First Saudi State in 1727. Today, the Diriyah giga-project is transforming the area around the historic At-Turaif District into a global destination for culture, heritage, dining and hospitality, inspired by traditional Najdi architecture.

name: Qiddiya
headline: A City Built Around Play
overview: Qiddiya City, about 45 km from downtown Riyadh, is being built as a destination for entertainment, sports and culture. Its first major attractions, Six Flags Qiddiya City and the Aquarabia water theme park, are now open to visitors.

name: The Red Sea
headline: Where the Desert Meets the Reef
overview: The Red Sea destination covers 28,000 km² of the western coast, with an archipelago of more than 90 islands. Developed by Red Sea Global, it welcomed its first guests in 2023 and is planned around regenerative tourism, with most of the archipelago left untouched.

name: AlUla
tagline: A living museum in the desert.
headline: Thousands of Years of Living History
overview: AlUla in north-west Saudi Arabia has been home to people for thousands of years, from the Dadanite and Lihyanite kingdoms to the Nabataeans. It is home to Hegra, the Kingdom's first UNESCO World Heritage Site, and is being developed by the Royal Commission for AlUla as a global destination for culture and nature.

kingdoms.name: Dadan
kingdoms.text: One of the most developed cities of the first millennium BCE in the Arabian Peninsula, on the incense trade route.

kingdoms.name: Lihyan
kingdoms.text: The Lihyanites ruled from Dadan after the Dadanites, leaving inscriptions and carved tombs in the cliffs.

kingdoms.name: The Nabataeans
kingdoms.text: The builders of Petra made Hegra their southern city and carved its monumental tombs into the sandstone.

landmarks.title: Elephant Rock
landmarks.text: Jabal AlFil, a giant sandstone formation shaped like an elephant, under one of the clearest night skies in the region.

landmarks.title: Maraya

name: King Salman Park
tagline: A green heart for the capital.

launch.caption: King Salman and the Crown Prince at the launch of four landmark Riyadh projects, including King Salman Park, in 2019.

headline: Nature in the Heart of Riyadh
overview: Built on the site of the former Riyadh Air Base, King Salman Park is planned as one of the largest urban parks in the world. It will bring green spaces, cultural venues and sports facilities to the heart of Riyadh, including the Royal Arts Complex.

name: ROSHN
headline: Homes for a New Generation
overview: ROSHN is a real estate developer owned by the Public Investment Fund. It builds integrated communities across the Kingdom, with homes, schools, mosques, parks and retail, and aims to house more than 2.2 million people by 2030.
